subject.title: [Feature]: Add a standard AISP/AISOP proposal contract for Skill Workshop

question: Should OpenClaw add a core-owned machine-readable Skill Workshop proposal contract, and if so should it be AISP/AISOP, an OpenClaw-native docs/tests fixture, or an external ClawHub/bundle-style artifact?
rationale: The current code already enforces the main lifecycle rules; the remaining choice sets product and security ownership for an optional contract artifact rather than fixing broken behavior.

options.title: Use OpenClaw-native docs/tests fixture
options.body: Define the lifecycle contract as a core-owned reference fixture or generated test input that mirrors existing service/schema behavior without adding an AISP runtime dependency.

options.title: Accept an AISP/AISOP reference artifact
options.body: Add an optional AISP/AISOP package only after deciding it is reference-only or validator-owned and cannot override service enforcement.

options.title: Move the package artifact outside core
options.body: Keep core to docs/tests and ask any AISP package to live as a ClawHub or bundle-style artifact unless a missing core API appears.

recommendation.title: Use OpenClaw-native docs/tests fixture
recommendation.body: Define the lifecycle contract as a core-owned reference fixture or generated test input that mirrors existing service/schema behavior without adding an AISP runtime dependency.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the central Skill Workshop proposal lifecycle, so they are the strongest history-based owner for the contract-authority question.
